rows.heading: # VisualCore — Fully Specified, Desktop-Driven iOS Graphics Suite
rows.note: D-01, D-02 (C-01, C-09): the 25-app suite edition is replaced by one app with 100 experiences. Carry its execution boundary: no signing, purchases, D3 OS change or publishing; Claude Desktop Code only.

rows.heading: ## Navigation
rows.note: Table of contents of the former README chapters 1-20. Replaced by the Auto-Creator.md outline (D-10); nothing to carry forward.

rows.heading: ## 1. Authoritative architecture and design corrections
rows.note: Header only. Authority passes to ADR-0009 and Auto-Creator.md (D-10, C-09). Rows 1.1-1.4 show what carries: most of VC-001..VC-020, the precedence order and the autonomy rule.

rows.heading: ### 1.1 Mission
rows.note: D-01 (C-01): '25 distinct products' become experiences of one app. Carry the dependency direction (experience, adapter, VisualCore, ANGLE host, Metal) and the rule to wrap, not rebuild, the ANGLE integration.

rows.heading: ### 1.2 Canonical decisions that supersede older advice
rows.note: VC-001..VC-020 stay binding except VC-002 and VC-003 (lock and 75 rows: D-07, D-08, C-04) and VC-005 (25 shippable targets: D-01, C-01). VC-014 narrows to the single product of D-03.

rows.heading: ### 1.3 Rules for conflicting material
rows.note: D-10 (C-09): keep the five-level order with Auto-Creator.md and CLAUDE.md in the README's place. Keep: an app manual beats the brainstorm; obsolete command syntax never deletes a requirement.

rows.heading: ### 1.4 What "unattended" means here
rows.note: Decide routine questions, record an ADR, proceed. Auto mode never overrides external permissions; scheduled tasks run only while Desktop is open and the Mac awake; checkpoints replace any promise of an endless session.

rows.heading: ## 2. Exact delivered scope and complete 25-app portfolio
rows.note: Header only. D-02: launch scope is 100 experiences; the 25 apps are the free experiences A01-A25. See rows 2.1-2.3.

rows.heading: ### 2.1 Core deliverables
rows.note: D-01, D-02 (C-01): framework, reference integration and Showcase are delivered (F00-F09 sealed); '25 app targets' become 25 free experiences; CI and the dormant device harness continue as UA-F10 and UA-F13.

rows.heading: ### 2.2 25 apps: original order and shared dependency waves
rows.note: Roster with capability and validity risk carries as A01-A25 (D-02); all 25 mandatory; default order 01 to 25 stays in the legacy ledger (D-12). Sealed so far: A01-A03 complete, A04 P00-P03.

rows.heading: ### 2.3 App success standards
rows.note: No-placeholder standard: working controls, the manual's core interaction and persistence, deterministic sample data, stress and error scenarios, accessibility fixtures. 'Identity' is now the experience id (D-06).

rows.heading: ## 3. Claude Desktop: bootstrap, permissions, and autonomous continuation
rows.note: Header only. Desktop-only execution, delegation limits and the checkpoint protocol still apply; see rows 3.1-3.4.

rows.heading: ### 3.1 Choose the right execution surface
rows.note: Local Desktop Code session on the project Mac; Auto permission mode, never Bypass; no UI automation to get past prompts or trust dialogs; Mac kept awake. The machine steps themselves live in setup.md.

rows.heading: ### 3.2 Desktop sessions versus the old Python supervisor
rows.note: The `claude -p` supervisor is history. Standing rules: one in-session worker, deterministic-only Python, file ledger, lease lock, failed stays failed. Its '263-gate ledger' is now one of two ledgers (D-12).

rows.heading: ### 3.3 Scope of standing delegation
rows.note: Routine engineering is delegated. Not delegated: resetting a dirty tree, deleting the ANGLE tree, updating D3, signing, agreements, purchases, IAP records, submission: BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION. Pushing follows D-13.

rows.heading: ### 3.4 Session/checkpoint protocol
rows.note: Each session: validate, status, next; claim a unique lease, never clear a lock blindly, release at the end; read one extracted manual, never the whole archive. The lease (claim/release) exists only in the legacy tool.

rows.heading: ## 4. Repository architecture and example file layout
rows.note: D-06, D-01, D-10, D-11 (after ADR-0003 and ADR-0004): two framework packages, experience packages, one app target, new document roles and spec numbers. Keep: XcodeGen spec, ignored .xcodeproj, no large binaries.

rows.heading: ### 4.1 Module contracts that must be proven with code
rows.note: Host, resources, effects, input and scenes, persistence, accessibility and diagnostics contracts exist with sealed tests (F02-F09, A01 phases). Audio and controller modules are still placeholders (ADR-0006).

rows.heading: ### 4.2 One writer, many reviewers
rows.note: At most 10 agents; one writer per file; the integration session owns specs, tasks, project.yml and bridge code; no concurrent Xcode builds or device jobs; an agent report never ticks a task: check the diff, rerun tests.

rows.heading: ## 5. Strict implementation-first schedule and stage gates
rows.note: Header only. Implementation before devices stays; the macro-sequence, lock and gate counts are replaced by the migration ledger order and ImplementationLock-100 (D-07, D-12, C-04).

rows.heading: ### 5.1 The only permitted macro-sequence
rows.note: D-07, D-08, D-12 (C-04): the order is now the migration ledger's, ending in ImplementationLock-100 and 300 rows. Keep: device commands pass guard-device first; a generic iOS build is a compile check, not a device test.

rows.heading: ### 5.2 Ten foundation gates (F00–F09)
rows.note: F00-F09 are sealed: evidence F00.json to F09.json, dossiers specs/001 to specs/010. Six {device} tasks (T-F418, T-F523, T-F613, T-F714, T-F810, T-F915) stay open; they were deferred to a campaign D-12 retires.

rows.heading: ### 5.3 Seven phases for EACH app (175 app gates)
rows.note: P00-P06 remain the legacy gates of A01-A25 (D-12; specs 011-185 per ADR-0004): 25 of 175 sealed, next A04-P04. Each X-A<nn> needs its seven gates. Store-listing parts of P06 fall away (C-06).

rows.heading: ### 5.4 Implementation lock: stricter than file counts
rows.note: D-07 (C-04): replaced by ImplementationLock-100 and its manifest (UA-F12). Keep: fresh full rerun, no skipped mandatory test, placeholder audit, no ProjectM or automation symbols in Release, a report with real commands.

rows.heading: ### 5.5 Repair during device qualification
rows.note: Record the failing test, smallest patch, rerun simulator checks and every affected device row, append evidence, never overwrite failures, no new features. Combine with UA-F12: any source change invalidates the lock.

rows.heading: ## 6. Spec Kit operation entirely within Desktop Code
rows.note: Header only. Spec Kit skills run inside the Desktop session, never through a CLI subprocess; see rows 6.1-6.3.

rows.heading: ### 6.1 Install/init without invoking Claude CLI
rows.note: Done once before F00: Spec Kit 1.4.1.dev0, claude integration, py scripts, nine skills (ADR-0001). No sealed check names the install or its event setting. Standing rule: never re-run `specify init` (setup.md).

rows.heading: ### 6.2 Invoke skills in the Desktop conversation, not terminal subprocesses
rows.note: Nine installed skills (converge included) run in the conversation. Order: specify, clarify, plan, checklist, tasks, analyze, implement, converge, then evidence and record. Tick a task only with a dated Verified line.

rows.heading: ### 6.3 Example app-specific prompt format
rows.note: Illustrative A08-P03 prompt of the old process. Real prompts are the archive's own, verbatim (ADR-0004), listed per feature in the prompt manifest; its lock wording now means ImplementationLock-100 (D-07).

rows.heading: ## 7. Shared renderer and ProjectM integration engineering
rows.note: Header only. The renderer seam and the ProjectM reference adapter are sealed (F02, F07); the preservation, isolation and measurement rules of 7.1-7.4 still bind (D-09).

rows.heading: ### 7.1 Preserve proven internals and fork provenance
rows.note: Forks stay pinned and read-only (pin in ADR-0005; clean-tree check sealed F02-F08). Never `git clean -fdx` inside them; engine changes only as logged upstream patches; build binaries with the reference's own scripts.

rows.heading: ### 7.2 Correct render/context lifecycle
rows.note: RenderHost state machine with context generations, sealed by F02 (.autonomy/evidence/F02.json; simulator runtimes 27.2 and 26.5). Real-device sweeps were deferred and remain unrun. AC-11.6 builds on it.

rows.heading: ### 7.3 Rendering independence and content
rows.note: No ProjectM ABI or preset loader in shared APIs, proven on link maps and symbols (scanners sealed F06, F08, F09); provenance for every shader and asset. 'Apps own code until reuse is proven' was replaced by ADR-0007.

rows.heading: ### 7.4 Performance lessons from original ProjectM tests
rows.note: Rules: store requests never block local UI; `async let` for independent startup work; pre-sorted indexes; load timed apart from the first frame; at least 200 samples per percentage gate. Its figures are ProjectM history.

rows.heading: ## 8. Product engineering, data, accessibility, security and release policy
rows.note: Header only. Domain, accessibility, StoreKit, privacy and compliance policies still bind every experience; see rows 8.1-8.4.

rows.heading: ### 8.1 Domain correctness
rows.note: Class rules for A01-A25: fixed step, units, reference fixtures, NaN policy; honest audio sources; cited datasets, no diagnosis; bounded untrusted input; no fake live wallpaper. 'Licensed models' collides with D-09.

rows.heading: ### 8.2 Native UX/accessibility
rows.note: SwiftUI/UIKit own UI, GPU owns imagery. Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels, automation ids, iPhone and iPad layouts, Reduce Motion and Flashing, non-color cues, real empty, denied and error states. Manual VoiceOver: D-08.

rows.heading: ### 8.3 StoreKit and privacy test discipline
rows.note: Matches D-04: no stored unlock flag, no synced _applicationInternalID, fake store under XCTest, SKTestSession for purchases and pending, no Apple Account in automation. Per-app privacy items become one set (UA-F11).

rows.heading: ### 8.4 Compliance and owner-only actions
rows.note: Public APIs only; scanner is live (scripts/check_compliance.py, sealed F01-F08); LGPL analysis; permissions are the owner's. Its 'no blanket network ban' is reversed by the offline rule of AC-15.2, with no ADR-0009 id.

rows.heading: ## 9. Dedicated Apple build-host environment
rows.note: Header only. The build host was verified and pinned in F00 (F00.json: verify_environment.py; Configs/toolchain.json); machine setup now lives in setup.md (D-10). See rows 9.1-9.3.

rows.heading: ### 9.1 Known owner Mac reference (historical, must reverify)
rows.note: Re-verified on this Mac in F00 and pinned: Xcode 27.2 (27B52), SDK 27.2, Swift 6.4.2, XcodeGen 2.46.0, CMake 4.4.5, runtimes 27.2 and 26.5 (F00.json, docs/verification/environment-F00.json). Never upgrade blindly.

rows.heading: ### 9.2 Preflight commands in Desktop's integrated terminal
rows.note: Preflight is scripted and sealed (F00.json, again in F02). Rules that stay: no placeholder strings in scripts, explicit timeouts, file-backed logs, no `tail` or `sort` pipes, device ids read without running tests.

rows.heading: ### 9.3 User's Windows host and macOS requirement
rows.note: Context of the owner's earlier Windows host. All work now runs locally on the project Mac, which setup.md assumes. Nothing else to carry forward.

rows.heading: ## 10. Fixed test-device inventory and supported capabilities
rows.note: Roster D1 iPhone15,4, D2 iPad17,3, D3 iPad15,7 is final (D-08). Never update D3 from iPadOS 26.5; claims only for tested models and OS; UDIDs stay private. F00 inventory: docs/verification/devices-observed.json.

rows.heading: ## 11. Single batched physical-device campaign — D1, then D2, then D3
rows.note: Header only. One batched campaign, D1 then D2 then D3, after the lock is kept by D-08; the scope is now 100 experiences per device (300 rows). See rows 11.1-11.5.

rows.heading: ### 11.1 Freeze the implementation first
rows.note: D-07, D-12: the guard is `scripts/migration_ledger.py guard-device` on ImplementationLock-100; the legacy guard can never pass. Keep: campaign run id, revision and toolchain fingerprint; a shared patch forces retests.

rows.heading: ### 11.2 Deterministic campaign schedule (75 mandatory rows)
rows.note: D-08 (C-04): 100 experiences per device, 300 rows, one install per device. Keep: fixed order, one row at a time, the per-row step sequence; a scenario may be not_applicable but the row itself stays mandatory.

rows.heading: ### 11.3 Concrete Apple tool commands (discover and verify current syntax)
rows.note: Templates for UA-F13: devicectl discovery, xcodebuild test with the hardware UDID (not the devicectl id), 180 s test allowance, xcresulttool summary, launch with VISUALCORE_AUTORUN, copy reports. Check flags with --help.

rows.heading: ### 11.4 In-app automation runner and testability
rows.note: Runner only under DEBUG || VISUALCORE_AUTOMATION, launch-environment trigger, writes JSON and exits, no symbols in shipping Release (nm). Framework runner and A01-A03 modes exist (sealed F09, A-gates); UA-F09 extends it.

rows.heading: ### 11.5 Device locking, system dialogs and true limitations
rows.note: A locked device, trust, permission prompt, signing, purchase sheet or picker is an owner prerequisite, not a defect. No input() waits: write BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION with the device and exact steps and leave the row open.

rows.heading: ## 12. All-app test matrix and device-specific acceptance
rows.note: Device minimums per experience A01-A25 plus the common row minimum (10-minute stress, 200 samples, traces, xcresult). Every mode also needs host or simulator proof before the lock. Ten-minute non-silent audio rule.

rows.heading: ## 13. Measurement, diagnostic artifacts and independent evidence
rows.note: Header only. Evidence structure, provenance, measurement method, test lessons and status words still apply; see rows 13.1-13.5.

rows.heading: ### 13.1 Evidence report structure
rows.note: Gate evidence JSON with run-check attestations is live in both ledger tools. Still to build: device fields (role, product type, OS, is_simulator=false, xcresult Passed) and scripts/verify_xcresults.py, never written.

rows.heading: ### 13.2 Source, build and runtime provenance
rows.note: Record commit and dirty flag, submodule pins, source hashes, tool versions, scheme, configuration, destination, signing mode, device type and OS build, run id, metrics. Raw bundles stay untracked; no UDID in Git.

rows.heading: ### 13.3 Performance methodology
rows.note: CADisplayLink interval counts; median, p95, p99; at least 200 samples per percentage gate; first run apart from warm runs; per-device quality tiers; size from thinning reports; container and defaults audit.

rows.heading: ### 13.4 XCTest and simulator lessons
rows.note: Test timeouts on (180 s); full output to a file; hang triage by elapsed time, screenshot, last started test; isolated simulators; privacy reset; erase only after saving. See docs/testing/simulator-test-lessons.md.

rows.heading: ### 13.5 Final reports and status words
rows.note: IMPLEMENTED, BUILT, SIMULATOR_VERIFIED, DEVICE_VERIFIED, READY_FOR_OWNER_RELEASE_REVIEW, BLOCKED or INCOMPLETE stay distinct and are never merged into one green label.

rows.heading: ## 14. Autonomous recovery, CI, Git and safety
rows.note: Header only. Git, CI, recovery and blocker rules still apply; pushing is frozen on the migration branch (D-13). See rows 14.1-14.11.

rows.heading: ### 14.1 Git and history
rows.note: LF endings; commit after each verified task or skill, feature ids in the subject; no trailers; the owner's Git identity; never reset, clean or rewrite history. Push: allowed 2026-11-10 (ADR-0007), frozen by D-13.

rows.heading: ### 14.2 CI design
rows.note: ci.yml has three jobs: checks, host tests, simulator build of the pure package (runs confirmed in F09). The wider graph and device-farm.yml are unbuilt; one target, not 25 (C-05, UA-F10). A build is never a device test.

rows.heading: ### 14.3 Recovery when Desktop session ends or runs out of context
rows.note: Resume from the ledgers, never from a chat summary: read CLAUDE.md, status and next, the relevant manual, Git state. Repair a half-done gate from the last passing commit; investigate a stale lock; bounded retries.

rows.heading: ### 14.4 External blockers and false-success prevention
rows.note: Blocker record: exact object, observed error, command, timestamp, safe operator action. Continue only work that respects gate order. Never waive a requirement, mark later gates green or bypass Apple or payment limits.

rows.heading: ### 14.5 Full ProjectM-iOS playbook adoption and suite-level execution policy (2026-11-10)
rows.note: Provenance note for the ProjectM-iOS playbook (SHA-256 8f691031...), once copied into the root CLAUDE.md; both are archived now (D-10, D-14). Its adapted rules are the rows from line 783 to 14.11.

rows.heading: #### Ownership, permissions, release decisions and source-of-authority
rows.note: Routine choices are delegated and recorded. ProjectM's push right, app id, product, price and waivers do not transfer. No invented waiver: keep the box, add the dated owner-ruling line. Owner-only list; no input() loops.

rows.heading: ### 14.6 Spec Kit playbook for every one of the 25 apps
rows.note: Research brief first, then the nine skills per feature: namespaced ids, {device} and {owner} tags, exact expected output per task, Verified lines, one commit per increment. Per-app target and bundle id fall away (D-01).

rows.heading: ### 14.7 Noninteractive repository setup, reproducible builds and release shape
rows.note: XcodeGen spec is the source of truth (now one app target: D-01, C-05). Signing.xcconfig include pattern; ids and names fixed before the first upload (OD-01, OD-02); valid framework version keys; pinned forks; provenance.

rows.heading: ### 14.8 CI and build-cost discipline
rows.note: Job order: docs, packages, cached XCFrameworks, host and simulator tests, generic iOS builds. Timeouts and concurrency per job; simulators picked by runtime; [skip ci] only for docs. GitHub runs wait on OD-04, OD-05.

rows.heading: ### 14.9 Mac, simulator and StoreKit automation lessons
rows.note: verify_environment.py before each session; full xcodebuild output to a file, 180 s test allowance; one simulator per lane; pricing lookup off the first frame. Its StoreKit 2 test-isolation rules belong in AC-14.

rows.heading: ### 14.10 Final hardware campaign and truthful release evidence
rows.note: D1, D2, D3, no interleaving; devicectl discovery; run_device_campaign.py with --dry-run; 200 samples; ten-minute non-silent audio proof; container audit; failures stay visible; pre-release checks. Now 300 rows (D-08).

rows.heading: ### 14.11 Playbook traceability and archive-integrity safeguard
rows.note: D-14, D-10: playbook and README now sit byte-identical under docs/archive/planning with a manifest and `planning_archive.py verify`. Keep: ProjectM permissions and waivers never transfer; evidence, not assertion.

rows.heading: ## 15. One-shot Claude Desktop launch prompt
rows.note: D-10 with D-01, D-07, D-08: the 25-app, 75-row launch prompt gives way to the continuation prompt. Keep: no CLI or model-calling Python, mandatory order, no fabricated pass, a deterministic ledger hand-over.

rows.heading: ## 16. Native Desktop scheduled-task continuation prompt
rows.note: D-10, D-07: the prompt names the README, 25 apps and IMPLEMENTATION-LOCK. Keep the mechanics: one local scheduled task, Auto mode, fires only while Desktop is open and the Mac awake, never clear a lock blindly.
